title: Eyes Up the Ribbon
hook: Yuna names the next sign. You drive.
scene: Overcast morning on I-5 south of the Core. You are alone in the Menace. The relay kit is lashed behind the seats — repeater, antenna, clamps. Yuna is on the radio, not in the cab. She names the interchange, the green panels, and the paint while you hold the right travel lane of three. You do not look down at the bumper to feel safe. The mountain is a gray smudge far east. This pavement is the Ribbon.
decision: Yuna is naming signs. Where do your eyes go?

options.text: Watch the bumper so you know you are still in the lane
options.result: You stare at the hood. A green panel goes by unread. Yuna has to say the exit twice. Eyes on the bumper is how you miss the highway you are already on.

options.text: Next sign, then the one after, then the paint and the gap
options.result: You take the next panel, then the one behind it, then the skip-dash. Yuna does not have to repeat the city. Eyes up named the Ribbon before you used it.

options.text: Watch the mountain so you know how far the climb still is
options.result: The mountain is a shape, not a road. You miss the I-90 split while you stare east. The schedule today stops at the valley floor. Eyes belong on the next sign.

options.text: Watch the radio so you do not miss a word she says
options.result: You look down at a speaker. The right lane starts to die into a ramp you did not name. Yuna can talk. Your eyes still have to own the pavement.

debrief: You watched the highway before you used it. Interchange, signs, paint, eyes up. Yuna stayed on the radio.

source.psdp_skill: Skill eleven: highway driving – part one
source.teaching_target: Highway observation first: interchanges, signs, and lane lines, eyes up, not on the bumper.
